gaps.sentence: He is very ___ about local history (KNOW).
gaps.explanation: 'Knowledgeable about something' means knowing a lot about it; it is the adjective form of 'knowledge'.

gaps.sentence: The airline is known for its excellent ___ (SERVE).
gaps.hint: noun needed after 'excellent'; note the spelling change
gaps.explanation: The noun of 'serve' is 'service' (-ice); a servant is a person who serves.

gaps.sentence: The company is a major ___ (EMPLOY) in the region.
gaps.hint: the company gives jobs — it is the one who employs
gaps.explanation: An employer gives work; an employee receives it. The sentence is about the company.

gaps.sentence: The audience found the lecture extremely ___ (BORE).
gaps.explanation: The lecture causes boredom, so it is boring; the audience would be bored.

gaps.sentence: She was ___ to accept the conditions at first (WILLING).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed: she did not want to
gaps.explanation: 'At first' suggests reluctance, so the negative adjective 'unwilling' (un- + willing) is needed.

gaps.sentence: He answered all the questions with great ___ (CONFIDENT).
gaps.explanation: 'Great' needs a noun: confidence. 'Confident' is the adjective.

gaps.sentence: The old factory will be ___ into flats (MODERN).
gaps.hint: verb needed in the passive (-ise); past participle
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ise forms the verb: modernise. The passive 'will be' needs the past participle 'modernised'.

gaps.sentence: When the costs rose, we had to ___ our plans (CONSIDER).
gaps.explanation: The prefix re- means again: reconsider means to think about something again. A base verb follows 'had to'.
